Subject: Running rights & output ownership clarifications — Order Form #ACME-172

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited. Procurement asked I surface a couple of questions folks want clarified in the order form prior to redlining:

1) Output ownership: Does Acme get exclusive title to outputs (responses, generated content) produced by the model when using our data and prompts? We need this spelled out for our productization plans.

2) Training / Model improvement: Can Redwood use Acme inputs/outputs as training data (even de-identified) for model improvement or does that require a separate opt-in?

3) Feedback license: Is there a generic feedback or telemetry license included that would let Redwood retain derived signals for product/benchmarking use?

We attached a short note from our legal team and the current draft order form (ACME-OF-172_initial_questions.pdf). Happy to do a 30-min call if that speeds things up — procurement would prefer everything resolved before vendor onboarding.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Running rights & output ownership clarifications — Order Form #ACME-172

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Assigning Sean and Grace to the thread for ops/product implications; looping in legal for contract language. Quick answers up front to keep momentum:

- Outputs: Our standard approach is that customers retain ownership of their customer content and the outputs derived directly from it. We can add explicit language in the order form that Acme owns outputs generated from your prompts and data.

- Training: By default Redwood uses aggregated, de-identified telemetry to improve system health and quality, but we recognize some customers require stricter controls. We can (A) offer a training-opt-out checkbox in the order form (no use for model training) or (B) allow a limited telemetry window for operational monitoring only.

- Feedback license: We typically request a non-exclusive feedback license to use anonymized signals and usage metrics for product improvement and diagnostics. We can narrow that to exclude any raw customer content or identifiable outputs.

I'm attaching a proposed redline that implements the opt-out checkbox and a tightened feedback clause. Suggested next steps: legal call Wed 5/13 11am PT to walk through language, followed by procurement's sign-off.

Attachments: RDW_proposed_orderform_redline_20260510.docx

If that path works, I'll ask Laura to draft the exact clauses and surface any gating issues.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Draft language for Acme — outputs, training, feedback

Team —

I reviewed Marissa's proposal and drafted two short clauses to put in the order form redline:

1) Output Ownership: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Outputs (defined as text, images, code, or other content generated by the Service in response to Customer-provided prompts and data)."

2) Training and Model Improvement: Option A (Customer Opt-Out): "Customer expressly elects not to permit Service Provider to use Customer Content or Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models. Service Provider may retain anonymized operational telemetry for a maximum of 30 days for debugging and capacity planning and will not use such telemetry for model training or research."

Option B (Default Narrow License): "Customer grants Service Provider a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to use de-identified and aggregated usage metrics and performance data for product improvement; Service Provider will not use raw Customer Content or identifiable Outputs to train core models without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Feedback License: Proposed minimal clause: "Customer grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated and de-identified Feedback (not including Customer Content or Outputs) for product development, benchmarking, and compliance purposes. Feedback will not include personal data or any data that could reasonably re-identify Customer or its end users."

Operational note from Grace (copied): restricting telemetry beyond 30 days will reduce our ability to diagnose intermittent regressions and may increase support cycles for major customers. Sean — pricing impact if customer picks Opt-Out?

I'll clean up the redline and send to Marissa; recommend we prepare fallback language (e.g., 90-day telemetry for operations, audit rights limited to SOC2 evidence only).

- Laura

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Pamela Cho <pam.cho@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex.reed@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Running rights & output ownership clarifications — Order Form #ACME-172

Marissa — appreciate the fast follow. We reviewed Redwood's draft clauses and Acme's legal position is as follows:

- Acme must retain exclusive ownership of Outputs. Please add explicit "assignment of output" language rather than a license.

- Redwood may retain operational telemetry for up to 90 days strictly for system stability; telemetry cannot be used for model training or research in any form without Acme's prior written consent.

- Feedback: Acme will permit a narrow, aggregated metrics license for Redwood to measure API success rates, latency, and anonymized error categories, provided that no raw or reconstructed Outputs are used.

- Audit & Evidence: before finalizing, Acme requires proof of SOC 2 Type II and a one-time upload of the data retention/configuration matrix (we attached a template). We prefer an explicit Docusign link for the final order form so procurement can route quickly.

We can accept the opt-out checkbox language but request the 90-day telemetry boundary be the default for our account. Can Redwood produce a final redline with these points by Monday 5/17? If so procurement will aim for signature the week of 5/24.

For reference, here is our preferred signature workflow: https://www.docusign.com/rdw-acme/ACME-OF-172.

Thanks,
Pamela Cho
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
